WHO WE ARE

A solution provider, built as a manufacturer.

Akura Engineering Services is a manufacturing company conforming to the ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System, acting as a solution provider to the customer's requirements for material handling.THE COMPANY, IN ITS OWN WORDS

Our vision

To become a highly effective, efficient and fast-moving organisation, where people are inspired to be the best for sustaining a growing network of customers, suppliers and stakeholders.

Our mission

To safely deliver varied products and projects within time, in any environment, for the benefit and complete satisfaction of our customers, shareholders, employees and the communities we serve.

WHAT WE STAND ON

Five values, applied to every order.

Anticipation

Reading the load, the floor and the next requirement before it is asked for.

Teamwork

One team carries an order from drawing through fabrication to dispatch.

Uniqueness

Frames adapted to the customer's drum, cylinder, bin or bay — not the other way round.

Reliability

Delivered on time, under warranty, and built to be used daily.

Accountability

We remain answerable for the product long after it leaves the works.

HOW WE BUILD

The engineering standard behind every frame.

Six principles govern what leaves the shop floor. They are the reason a trolley built here is still in service after the third shift pattern changes.

High durability

Sections and welds specified for continuous industrial duty, not intermittent use.

Rust-free surface coating

Treated and coated finishes that hold up in chemical, coastal and wash-down environments.

Bearing-fitted wheels

Quality wheels on bearings, matched to floor surface and load, so effort stays low.

Load bearing capacity

Rated frames tested against the working load, with margin designed in.

Ergonomic frames

Handle heights, tilt angles and grip points set around the operator's body.

Value for money

In-house manufacture removes the trading margin between design and delivery.

THE RANGE

Eleven families. Fifty-three products.

The catalogue is organised by the job rather than the product, because that is how a plant describes its problem. Every unit is available in multiple colours and can be adapted to customer drawings.
